headline: GOLD SLIPS TO $4,444: Iran Military Strikes Revive Oil Shock Fears, Silver Drops 2.5%
snippet: Spot gold dropped to $4,444 on May 26–27 as renewed U.S. strikes on Iranian targets pushed Brent crude back above $95/bbl, stoking inflation fears and strengthening the dollar. Silver shed 2.5% to $76.08, extending a ~20% retreat from the $87 high hit on tariff-deal optimism earlier this month.

headline: DOE TAPS OKLO TO CONVERT WEAPONS PLUTONIUM INTO REACTOR FUEL; Stock Jumps 11%
snippet: The U.S. DOE selected Oklo and four other firms on May 26 for advanced negotiations to convert up to 20 metric tonnes of surplus warhead plutonium into fuel for advanced nuclear reactors. Sam Altman-backed Oklo surged 11% on the announcement; the program could reshape SMR fuel economics and domestic nuclear supply chains.

headline: COPPER PORPHYRY CONFIRMED: Kobrea Drills 2,358m at El Perdido, Argentina — Core Still Untested
snippet: Kobrea Exploration (CSE: KBX) completed a 6-hole, 2,358m Phase 1 drill program at El Perdido in Mendoza, Argentina on May 26, confirming a large hydrothermal Cu-Au-Mo porphyry system. Geological data shows alteration and sulphide intensity strengthening with depth — with the core of the system still untested ahead of Phase 2.

headline: GR SILVER SHATTERS RECORDS: 45.1m at 1,623 g/t Ag at San Marcial — Incl. 8.25m at 8,579 g/t
snippet: GR Silver Mining's hole SMS26-04 at Mexico's San Marcial deposit returned the company's strongest intercept in its history: 45.1 metres at 1,623 g/t silver, including a jaw-dropping 8.25m at 8,579 g/t Ag. Two rigs are active with two more en route; a full 20,000m step-out campaign is underway and a resource update is expected H2 2026.

headline: AYA GOLD HITS BEST INTERCEPT EVER at Boumadine: 890 g/t AgEq Over 51.5 Metres in Morocco
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver's Boumadine project in Morocco produced its strongest intercept on record: 890 g/t AgEq (2.05 g/t Au, 535 g/t Ag, 3.8% Zn, 5.9% Pb) over 51.5 metres, just 70m below the current pit shell. With 11 rigs active and 69,000m drilled year-to-date, an updated PEA is expected mid-2026.

headline: BALD HILL BACK: MinRes Restarts Australian Lithium Mine After 18 Months on Ice
snippet: Mineral Resources launched ramp-up operations at its 165,000 dmt/yr Bald Hill spodumene mine in Western Australia this week, ending an 18-month care-and-maintenance shutdown. First concentrate production targets July 2026 and first export shipment Q1 FY27. The restart was triggered by lithium carbonate recovering to CNY 180,000/t, up from the lows that halted output in late 2024.

headline: SILVER DEFICIT HITS YEAR SIX — GoldSilver.com: 'Stop Chasing the Number' Near $74
snippet: After silver spiked to $87 on tariff-truce optimism before retreating to $74, GoldSilver.com cautions against chasing: the gold-silver ratio compressed from 62:1 to 55:1 in a single week — historically a signal to reassess. The structural bull case remains intact with six consecutive annual supply deficits totalling ~762M oz; J.P. Morgan still targets $90 silver in Q4 2026.

headline: GOLD AT $4,400, MINERS AT 0.7x NAV: Analysts Say Junior Equities 'Decades Behind' the Metal
snippet: Despite gold holding above $4,400, most gold producers and developers trade at 0.7–0.9× NAV versus bull-market historical averages of 1.2–1.5×. Analysts cite persistent institutional underallocation to junior miners, sector-wide operational leverage at today's margins, and rising M&A activity as three catalysts for a valuation catch-up trade.

headline: MP MATERIALS CUTS ALL CHINA SALES, Posts Record Q1: NdPr Revenue Up 117%, Independence Live
snippet: MP Materials posted record Q1 2026 NdPr production (917t, +63% YoY) and sales (1,006t, +117%), with Adjusted EBITDA swinging to positive $36.6M. In a strategic pivot, the company ceased all China sales and redirected its entire Mountain Pass output to the U.S. supply chain, underpinned by a $400M DoD investment in its Independence magnet facility in Fort Worth.

headline: RARE EARTH PRICES PAUSE After 160% YTD Rally — China's June Mining Quota Is the Next Catalyst
snippet: NdPr oxide pulled back 21% in April to ~$99/kg — its steepest monthly retreat since the Q1 surge — though NdPr remains 88% above January levels. Analysts forecast a $95–$115/kg consolidation range ahead of China's MIIT mid-year mining quota announcement, expected in June, which is seen as the next major inflection point for Western rare earth equities.

headline: COPPER RETREATS FROM $6.65 RECORD to $6.20 as Iran Oil Risk Squeezes Manufacturing Demand
snippet: Copper futures held near $6.20/lb as of May 25, sustaining a pullback from May 13's record $6.65 — with elevated Middle East energy costs squeezing manufacturing margins and tempering demand. Analysts remain structurally bullish long-term, citing AI data-centre wiring and clean-energy electrification as demand floors that keep the copper thesis intact.
